security_problem: Round-5 P1/P2: a hot reload that introduces or updates a stdio attestation pin re-resolves mutable launcher/payload paths and can attest an on-disk replacement as the identity of the already-running child (server_attested=true for an unrelated running server); and a call that releases runtimeMu before blocking for approval combines the captured policy snapshot with live mutable resolved-identity state after release, so a reload can make an allowed or denied terminal event report the wrong resolved digest or attested=false even though the call passed the old pin.
required_behavior: A configured stdio invocation identity is resolved exactly once at proxy construction from the logical server policy current at startup: the resolved launcher, literal argv, and only the policy-declared entry payload positions are bound exactly as in round 4, and the resolution contract (attestation kind plus normalized entry_arg_positions, sorted copy) is cached immutable for the proxy/stdio-child lifecycle. Hot reload never re-hashes launcher or payload paths and never re-resolves identity: unrelated policy/redactor/audit/approval reloads remain atomic, and same-shape digest comparisons use the cached startup digest. A pin introduced after an unattested start publishes but has no startup contract, so tools/call denies as unresolved/restart-required and never invokes the resolver. A same-shape digest replacement compares against the cached startup digest and denies on mismatch until restart. A changed kind or entry-position resolution shape cannot reuse the cached digest even when the expected digest string is equal, and denies until restart. Removing attestation may restore explicit unattested behavior; an originally unattested process remains unresolved on later reintroduction. A resolution failure at startup stays unresolved for the lifecycle and is not retried on reload. Every approval terminal allow/deny, receipt evidence, and taint mutation uses one complete runtime snapshot containing policy, redactor, approval backend/timeout, resolved identity state, resolution contract, and claimed server metadata; no post-release terminal path reads live mutable identity fields. All 11 canonical registry-runner rejects, negative controls, entry-artifact-not-transitive boundary, no-attestation zero-work, no argument leak on identity denial, approval policy/timeout/receipt/taint snapshots, and confused-deputy demo behavior are preserved.
failure_behavior: Fail closed for tools/call when attestation is configured and startup identity evidence is absent, incompatible, unresolved, or mismatched; never re-hash mutable launcher/payload paths during reload; never re-resolve identity during reload; never combine a captured policy snapshot with live mutable identity state on a post-approval terminal path.
non_goals: attesting a process whose executable or transitive dependencies changed after measurement
identity attestation without an explicit invocation snapshot
imprecise or non-injective artifact identity encoding
attesting a server name without binding to the measured process snapshot
trusting MCP-declared server metadata as identity proof

attack_classes.expected: missing, unsupported, mismatched, stale, or mixed-generation identity attestation denies tools/call with zero relay and never reports server_attested=true
